title: power-scenarios.json contract
description: Structural contract for <module>/Verification/simulation-plan/power-scenarios.json — one entry per scenario materialized from references/power-scenarios-template.md's standard set. Read by power-analysis alone, and these two fields are exactly what it reads: it keys SAIF and PT-PX reports by id and groups runs by sequence_ref. The standard set's abstract columns (clock / reset / data / low-power state, the scenario name, its purpose) are NOT here: no program reads them, so they belong in verification-plan.md §4 beside the per-scenario materialization note that explains them. sequence_ref resolving against sequences.json is not expressible here; the check-scaffold gate enforces it, where both files are in hand. minItems is 1 because an empty table is not a module with no power question: power-analysis runs it, measures nothing, and returns a pass whose power_by_scenario is empty — a stage that reports success for work it did not do. The standard set above is 8 rows, and a row you drop is a note in verification-plan.md, not a row removed from here.

id.description: The standard set's scenario id (S1 … S7, or S8+ for a supplement). Every SAIF file and PT-PX report directory is named after it, and power-analysis's result.json keys its per-scenario rows by it.

sequence_ref.description: A sequences.json entry's name. emit_power_tests groups by this and runs each group once, so two scenarios that reduce to the same RTL stimulus are the same measurement: declare one of them, not both.
